bug_info.bug_desc: Before the fix, fatal alerts unconditionally cleared all status and trigger bits. In aes_control_fsm, alert_fatal_i directly forced idle, stall, output_lost, output_valid, and input_ready to 0 while forcing their write-enables high, and also forced the start, key/IV/data-in clear, data-out clear, and PRNG-reseed trigger write-enables. In aes_core, alert_fatal_o forced the recoverable control-update error status bit to be cleared by driving hw2reg.status.alert_recov_ctrl_update_err.d to 0 when a fatal alert occurred. This destroys valuable debug/status information whenever any fatal alert is asserted, including the recoverable control-update error indication, and it is not configurable. The root cause is that fatal-alert-driven status/trigger clearing was hard-coded rather than being controlled by a compile-time option.
bug_info.fix_hint: Add a package-level parameter such as ClearStatusOnFatalAlert with a default of 1'b0, and create a local clear_on_fatal signal equal to that parameter ANDed with the fatal-alert indicator. Use clear_on_fatal in aes_control_fsm for all status and trigger forced-clearing assignments, and in aes_core for gating the recoverable control-update error status bit's d/de signals. This keeps the old clearing behavior only when explicitly enabled, while preserving status and trigger state by default for debugging.
